mil7.7.2:1.1: “Sir Nagasena, you said ‘one quality of the child at the breast is to be taken up’—what is that one quality to be taken up”?
mil7.7.2:1.2: “Just as, Great King, a child at the breast clings to what is good for it, and one who longs for milk cries;
mil7.7.2:1.3: so too, Great King, a practitioner who exercises spiritual effort should hold to what is good for him, and should be endowed with knowledge of the Dhamma in everything: in exposition, in questioning, in right effort, in solitude, in the company of the worthy, in cultivating good friendship.
mil7.7.2:1.4: This, Great King, is the one quality of the child at the breast to be taken up.
mil7.7.2:1.5: This was said, Great King, by the Blessed One, the god of gods, in the Long Collection, in the discourse on final extinguishment—
mil7.7.2:2.1: ‘Come along, Ananda, strive for the essential goal, devote yourselves to the essential goal, and abide diligent, ardent, and resolute in it’”.
mil7.7.2:3.1: The Child At the Breast, second.
